text:
emily_support: Customer C-7890 opened a ticket right after rolling python-sdk 1.35.0. They see intermittent 401s (~1-3% of requests) and p95 latency jumping from ~120ms to ~480ms. Started immediately after deploy.

rahul_sdk: can you paste the client init and a minimal repro? is this the sync client in threaded workers? any custom retry/backoff configured?

emily_support: sync client in a ThreadPoolExecutor, high concurrency. sanitized snippet:
```
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'])

def call_one():
    return client.responses.create(model='gpt-4o-mini', input='ping')

with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=80) as ex:
    futures = [ex.submit(call_one) for _ in range(2000)]
    [f.result() for f in futures]
```
Logs show:
```
HTTPError: 401 Unauthorized
  File "redwood/http.py", line 128, in send
  note: token refresh attempted concurrently; some threads still received 401
```
Downgrade to redwood==1.34.2 reportedly stops the failures.

rahul_sdk: thanks, that aligns with a refactor landed in 1.35.0 — we switched to per-thread short-lived sessions and moved token refresh to an async callback without a proper lock guard. Under heavy concurrency, concurrent refreshes can race and clobber the cached token, producing a small window where valid requests use a stale token and receive 401s, which then inflates latency due to retries.

kevin_prod: reproduced on a small canary by simulating a secret rotation; observed ~2% 401s and noticeable p95 tail increase. Repro is deterministic with concurrent threads + mid-run key change.

rahul_sdk: immediate mitigation: pin to redwood==1.34.2 and set REDWOOD_SDK_REFRESH_LOCK=1 in the environment to restore legacy refresh locking. I will open a hotfix PR (target: 1.35.1) to add a compare-and-set guard around the async refresh and reintroduce the refresh lock for the sync client path. ETA 3-6 hours if CI passes.

emily_support: notified the customer with the pin + env var workaround. They applied the pin and set the env var; initial monitoring shows errors stopped. Customer requested a formal patch release timeline and a backport note for release notes.

alice_engineering: please add a deterministic integration test for CI: spawn 50-100 worker threads, rotate the API key during the run, and assert zero 401s. Also test streaming/async clients and the scenario with K8s secret refresh.

rahul_sdk: will add repro script and integration test under sdk/tests/integration/test_refresh_race.py and a stress job in CI. PR will include the explanation, fix, and instructions for using REDWOOD_SDK_REFRESH_LOCK until 1.35.1 ships.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-988 (severity P2). Link: https://incidents.internal/redwood/INC-2026-988

kevin_prod: note for changelog: "1.35.0 changed session pooling and token refresh internals. If you observe intermittent 401s under high concurrency, pin to 1.34.2 or set REDWOOD_SDK_REFRESH_LOCK=1 until 1.35.1 is released."

emily_support: closing the support case after customer confirms stability post-pin. Will reopen if regression recurs.

rahul_sdk: tagging @alice_engineering and @kevin_prod to validate streaming & async flows once the patch lands.
